land.text: Castile, united for good with León in 1230

predecessors.note: The Kingdom of Castile dossier ends in 1235 and names this state as its successor; the Crown page dates the permanent union of Castile and León to 23 September 1230 and the Crown from 1230. Cliopatria's Crown of Castile row starts in 1236 with the conquest of Córdoba, which is where this dossier starts. León's land (León, Galicia and the León-Extremadura marches) arrives through this predecessor, not directly: kingdom-of-leon ends in December 1230 merging into kingdom-of-castile, its only successor, and Cliopatria's Kingdom of León row to 1235 lies inside this state's 1236 shape (1,147 of its 1,178 cells are Castile plus León of 1235). kingdom-of-leon is therefore no longer listed as a predecessor (eu-12-l repair, 2026-10-25).

land.text: the Crown of Castile (with Granada, the Canaries, the Indies and Navarre), whose throne Charles took in 1516

successors.note: Charles I was proclaimed king of Castile with his mother Joanna after Ferdinand II died in 1516 (Crown page: 23 January 1516; the list of monarchs: 13 March 1516). The Crown page keeps the Crown of Castile in being to the Nueva Planta decrees of 1716; the map follows Cliopatria and ends this state in 1515.

capitals.name: Toledo
capitals.note: The pages give no capital: 'Capital: No settled capital' (Kingdom of Castile infobox), 'Castile didn't have a permanent capital', with Burgos, Valladolid and Toledo named in a footnote as 'centres of royal authority'. Toledo, the most central, stands for the whole life; the court was itinerant, and Alfonso X died at Seville. Madrid (1561-1601) and Valladolid (1601-1606) lie after this state's end.

rulers.name: Ferdinand III
rulers.note: Reigned from 30 August 1217; to 30 May 1252. Union of Castile and León 1230.

rulers.name: Peter (the Cruel)
rulers.note: To 23 March 1369: killed by Henry at Montiel.

rulers.name: Henry II (Trastámara)
rulers.note: To 29 May 1379; the House of Trastámara 'ruled Castile from 1369 to 1504' (Kingdom of Castile page).

rulers.name: John II
rulers.note: To 21 July 1454; Ferdinand of Antequera was regent during the minority.

rulers.name: Ferdinand V (the Catholic)
rulers.title: co-monarch with Isabella
rulers.note: From 15 January 1475; also Ferdinand II of Aragon.

rulers.name: Joanna I (the Mad)
rulers.note: Queen to 1555 on the page's list; her son Charles I became co-monarch on 13 March 1516.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1236 shape without Jaén and Arjona, for 1236-1240

keyframe_review.note: 311,118 km2 for 1236-1240: Castile plus León of 1235 (1,147 of 1,178 cells) and Córdoba, 'the old Umayyad capital of Córdoba in 1236'. The Crown page gives about 335,000 km2 in 1300 (the 1294 shape is 353,152 km2, ratio 1.05; this earlier shape is 0.93 of the 1300 figure, which fits the later gains). The shape already holds the Jaén district (12 cells within 40 km of Jaén) though the Ferdinand III page has Arjona taken in 1244 and Jaén surrendered only in 1246: the two towns are removed. Baeza, Andújar and Martos (Castilian-occupied from 1225 in the Kingdom of Castile dossier) stay.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape without Seville, Jaén and Arjona, for 1241-1243

keyframe_review.note: 324,364 km2 for 1241-1249: 52 cells are added at 1241, 51 of them taken from Cliopatria's Almohad shape: the Huelva-Niebla district (Niebla and Huelva 'in 1238', a client), the Campiña between Córdoba and Seville (Écija-Estepa-Lucena line), and seven cells in a ring round Seville. The pages date Seville to 22 December 1248, Arjona to 1244 and Jaén to March 1246, so in 1241-1243 Seville, Jaén and Arjona are not Castile's. The Campiña cells are on no page opened (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: the 1241 shape with Arjona added, without Seville and Jaén

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1244-1245: Ferdinand III 'captured Arjona in 1244' (Emirate page; 'Arjona, Mula and Lorca in 1244' on the Ferdinand III page). Jaén and Seville still outside.

correction.text: the 1241 shape without Seville, for 1246-1247

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1246-1247: the Treaty of Jaén (March 1246) hands Jaén to Ferdinand III; Seville falls only in December 1248.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1241 shape, unchanged, for 1248-1249

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1248-1249: 'on 22 December 1248, Ferdinand III entered as a conqueror in Seville'; the full 1241 outline then holds to 1249.

354,308 km2 for 1250-1259: 116 cells are added (counted against the neighbours' 1249 shapes: 39 from Cliopatria's Almohad shape, Murcia 31, Dénia and Valencia 21, Córdoba 8, Almería 6, Niebla 4, Granada 3). Murcia and Orihuela came 'by the famous pact of Alcaraz' (1243) as a client kingdom until 1266, so those cells are drawn as a vassal tint by the ledger, not as direct land; Almizra (26 March 1244) fixed the Murcian boundary with Aragon. 'The boundaries of the new Castilian state established by Ferdinand III remained nearly unchanged' until the late fifteenth century.

354,283 km2 for 1260-1284: one Alicante cell lost. 'In 1261 Alfonso X captured Jerez'; Niebla 'in 1262'; Murcia annexed in 1266 after the 1264-1266 revolt. The page says Alfonso 'returned Algarve to the King of Portugal' in 1263 (treaty of Badajoz 1267); no shape holds the Algarve.

352,700 km2 for 1285-1293: seven cells on the Aragonese frontier near Valencia and Requena lost, two gained near Alicante. No page opened dates this adjustment; the Torrellas page says the succession dispute followed Alfonso X's death in 1284 (unverified: page budget).

353,152 km2: one Strait cell gained (Tarifa, October 1292), two cells near Cádiz drop out (one passes to Granada's shape). The year 1294 is Cliopatria's; the Emirate page dates Tarifa to October 1292.

352,987 km2 for 1305-1332 (Crown page: about 335,000 km2 in 1300, ratio 1.05). The treaty was signed 'on 9 August 1304' and the border finalised 'the following year' (1305): Aragon was awarded 'many cities north of the Segura' and Castile was 'restored' the Kingdom of Murcia except the part conquered earlier. Cliopatria's change is five Alicante-Vinalopó cells gained and five lost (four on the Requena-Utiel line, one near Alicante); the page names no city, so the Alicante gain cannot be checked and may belong to Aragon (gap for a reader of the Spanish page on the Sentencia de Torrellas). Gibraltar, Castilian from 1309 to 17 June 1333, is not in the shape; the ledger carries it (gain 1309, loss June 1333).

354,049 km2 for 1333-1343: five cells on the northern Granada frontier (-5.3 to -4.9 E, 37.0 to 37.2 N, the Olvera-Teba line) gained, one near Málaga lost. The Alfonso XI page was silent, but the Muhammad IV of Granada page dates the line: 'the capture of Olvera, in June 1327', Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime after it, and Teba 'the fortress surrendered on 30 August' 1330. The shape is therefore six and three years late for those cells (ledger events of 1327 and 1330); the assignment of the five cells to these towns is my reading. Gibraltar, which Castile lost on 17 June 1333 (ledger), is outside this shape as it was outside the shapes before it. (Repaired by eu-12-l, 2026-10-25.)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1333 shape, unchanged, but its five Olvera-Teba cells hold from 1327 (Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte, Torre Alháquime) and 1330 (Teba); Gibraltar, held 1309 to June 1333, is outside the shape
Cliopatria's 1344 shape, unchanged, holding from 1342 (Priego, Alcalá la Real); Algeciras from 26 March 1344

keyframe_review.note: 355,736 km2 for 1344-1351: seven cells from Granada (the Priego-Alcalá la Real line and two on the Cádiz coast and the Strait). Castile took Priego and Alcalá la Real in 1342 (Emirate page) and Algeciras on 26 March 1344; the shape is unchanged but starts in 1342.
356,007 km2: one eastern cell near 37.7 N, -3.0 E gained from Granada; no page opened mentions it (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1363 shape plus the eight 1352-outline cells it removes, for 1363-1369

keyframe_review.note: 369,605 km2 for 1363-1374: 58 cells in Aragon and Valencia are added ('In 1363, Castile continued the war against Aragon, and again occupied Tarazona'; then Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe and Morvedre; 'The Castilians penetrated the Kingdom of Valencia in 1363, and conquered Alicante, Caudete, Elda, Gandia, and other places'), and eight Granada-edge cells are given back. No page returns Priego or Alcalá la Real to Granada, so the 1352 cells stay. The page ends the war in 1369, so the occupation cannot be held to 1374; it holds 1363-1369 (Algeciras excepted from 1369).

correction.text: the 1352-1362 outline without Algeciras

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1370-1374: the page gives the war's end as 1369 ('Peter of Castile was finally overthrown in 1369'), so the Aragonese lands drop out, and 'Muhammed V, Sultan of Granada, took the opportunity to recapture Al-Jazeera Al-Khadra' (Algeciras, 1369; Siege of Algeciras page). Biscay, 1370 on the Crown page, is already inside the 1236 outline.

356,007 km2 for 1375-1394, the 1352 outline again. Algeciras was Granada's from 1369 until the Moors destroyed the city in 1379 (Siege of Algeciras page), so the Algeciras cell is premature in 1375-1378; no other change.
356,056 km2 for 1395-1401: no cell changes, the outline is only re-traced (116 vertices); no event.

357,369 km2 for 1402-1406: four cells of Lanzarote are added ('in the summer of 1402'; Jean de Béthencourt and Gadifer de la Salle); two cells on the Granada frontier swap. The islands were held under a seigneurial pact of vassalage to the Crown, not by the Crown.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1407 shape, unchanged, holding from 1405

keyframe_review.note: 360,030 km2 for 1407-1414: nine cells added (Fuerteventura 8, El Hierro 1). 'The conquest of the island was completed in 1405' (Fuerteventura) and El Hierro 'took place in 1405', two years before the shape.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1415 shape, unchanged, holding from 1410

keyframe_review.note: 360,277 km2 for 1415-1439: one cell at Antequera gained. 'He conquered the town of Antequera (1410)', five years before the shape.
360,768 km2 for 1440-1462: two cells gained and one lost on the north-eastern Granada edge (37.8 N, -2.9 to -2.5 E); no page opened dates it (unverified: page budget).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1463 shape, unchanged, holding from August 1462

keyframe_review.note: 361,914 km2 for 1463-1481: five cells on the Gibraltar-Algeciras coast gained. 'Moorish rule over Gibraltar came to an end in August 1462', a year before the shape.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1482 shape plus Alhama de Granada (February 1482); Gran Canaria from 29 April 1483

keyframe_review.note: 364,321 km2 for 1482-1486: seven cells added (Gran Canaria 6, La Gomera 1). 'On 29 April 1483 Guayarmina Semidán surrendered at Ansite Fortress', so Gran Canaria is Castilian only from 1483; Alhama de Granada, taken in February 1482, is not in the shape. La Gomera was ceded in 1477 by Inés Peraza and Diego García de Herrera to their son under their fiefdom, with no conquest date on the page.

correction.text: the 1482 shape plus Alhama, Ronda and Marbella

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1485: Ronda and Marbella fall (Granada War page).

correction.text: the 1482 shape plus Alhama, Ronda, Marbella and Loja

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1486: Loja after the 'second Loja siege' (the page gives the siege year, not the surrender).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1487 shape, unchanged, holding 1487-1489

keyframe_review.note: 377,486 km2 for 1487-1491: 48 cells from Granada (Ronda, Marbella, Málaga, Vélez-Málaga, Loja, Alhama) added at 1487. Vélez-Málaga capitulated on 27 April 1487 and Málaga on 18 August 1487; the shape holds 1487-1489, after which Baza and the east fall.

union.text: the eastern emirate around Baza, Guadix and Almería

correction.text: the 1487 shape plus Baza, Guadix and Almería

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1490-1491: the eastern emirate (Baza after a six-month siege begun in 1489; Almería and Guadix through al-Zagal) is added before the surrender of Granada on 2 January 1492.

390,719 km2 for 1492-1496: 53 cells added (Almería 29, Granada 15, Lorca fringe 8) after 'the city capitulated on January 2, 1492' ('Boabdil surrendered Granada to Ferdinand and Isabella'). The infobox of the war reads 'Granada annexed to Castile'. The Crown page's table lists '1492: Granada and the Indies'.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1497 shape, unchanged, with the Canary part holding from 1493-1496 and Hispaniola from 1496

keyframe_review.note: 412,242 km2 for 1497-1501: about 70 cells of Hispaniola around Santo Domingo and ten Canary cells (La Palma 3, Tenerife 7) are added. La Palma's conquest ended on 3 May 1493 and Tenerife's on 25 July 1496 (Canary page); 'the city of Santo Domingo was founded in 1496 by Christopher Columbus's brother Bartholomew' (Spanish Empire page); Melilla was conquered in 1497 (not in the shape).

417,013 km2 for 1502-1506: 22 cells of western Hispaniola added; no page opened dates the western Hispaniola settlement (unverified: page budget; confidence-1 event). Re-checked in the eu-12-l repair: the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo page is silent on western Hispaniola (Ovando governor from 1502 only).

479,840 km2 for 1507-1511: 297 cells added, almost all of the rest of Hispaniola (381 of its 385 gazetteer cells are now inside) and four cells at Oran. The Spanish Empire page says only 'between 1505 and 1510'; the Mers El Kébir page dates Mers el-Kebir to 1505 ('captured it in 1505 under Cardinal Cisneros') and the Spanish Oran page dates Oran to 1509 ('Spanish conquest: 1509'). The four Oran cells are therefore Mers el-Kebir alone for 1507-1508 and both towns from 1509; no cell is split between them. The page does not describe the settlement of the rest of Hispaniola (unverified: page budget; confidence-1 events). (Repaired by eu-12-l, 2026-10-25.)

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1507 shape, unchanged, but its four cells at Oran hold Mers el-Kebir from 1505 and Oran from 1509 (the shape has them 2 years early for Oran)
Cliopatria's 1512 shape, unchanged, with Puerto Rico holding from 1508, Jamaica from 1509, Darién from 1510, eastern Cuba from 1511 and Navarre from 1512

keyframe_review.note: 535,550 km2 for 1512-1515: 225 cells added, namely Puerto Rico (45 of its 47 gazetteer cells), all of Jamaica (51), the eastern end of Cuba (41 cells), 20 cells of Darién, the rest of Navarre (39 of 41 cells now inside, 6 already since 1496), and a handful on the Algerian coast and at Tripoli (13.5 E). Dates on the pages: Puerto Rico 'conquered ... (1508)', Santa María la Antigua del Darién 'settled by Vasco Núñez de Balboa in 1510', '1512: Navarre' (Crown page table), the North African posts only 'between 1505 and 1510'; Jamaica and eastern Cuba were dated by the eu-12-l repair (Jamaica settled 1509, Colony of Santiago page; Baracoa by August 1511, Velázquez page); Tripoli is dated 1510 on the Spanish Tripoli page but as Aragonese (Sicily). Puerto Rico, Jamaica, Darién and eastern Cuba are therefore in the shape one to four years late, and Navarre starts in 1512. The overseas cells make this shape larger than the 335,000 km2 of 1300 by construction.

ledger.note: 1236: Ferdinand III takes Córdoba; Castile and León, united for good in 1230, are drawn as the Crown of Castile. 'the old Umayyad capital of Córdoba in 1236'; 'The resulting treaty of Benavente was signed on 11 December 1230'. The year is Cliopatria's start; the pages date the union to 1230 and Córdoba to 1236 without a day.

region.text: 'the old Umayyad capital of Córdoba in 1236'

ledger.note: 1236: Córdoba is conquered. The page names no holder; Cliopatria's Taifa of Córdoba row (1147-1249) is the nearest dossier.

1238: Niebla and Huelva come under Castile as a client. The Ferdinand III page lists 'Niebla and Huelva in 1238' among his acquisitions and says Niebla was 'absorbed' only 'in 1262': the interval as a client is my reading.

region.text: 'Orihuela and Murcia in 1243 (by the famous 'pact of Alcaraz')'

ledger.note: 1243: Murcia and Orihuela accept Castilian protection by the pact of Alcaraz. The page says Murcia was 'received and organized as vassal states under Muslim governors'; the Murcia page: 'roughly two decades as a protectorate of the Crown of Castile'. The Treaty of Almizra (26 March 1244) 'delineated the Murcian boundary with James I of Aragon'.

region.text: Arjona, captured by Ferdinand III in 1244

ledger.note: 1244: Ferdinand III captures Arjona (the Ferdinand III page: 'Arjona, Mula and Lorca in 1244').
1246: Jaén surrenders under the Treaty of Jaén (March 1246).

1246: Granada becomes Ferdinand III's vassal. The Treaty of Jaén (March 1246): Ibn al-Ahmar agreed 'to surrender Jaén and to become Ferdinand's vassal', with a twenty-year truce. The Ferdinand III page dates a 'tributary arrangement from Granada' to 1238 and the Nasrid page 'tribute-paying vassals from 1243'; later treaties raised the tribute (150,000 maravedíes in 1246, 250,000 after the 1264-1266 revolt, twelve thousand doubloons in 1344). The vassalage was broken in war years (1264, 1340, 1405-1410): drawn as one span.

region.text: 'on 22 December 1248, Ferdinand III entered as a conqueror in Seville'

ledger.note: 1248: Ferdinand III enters Seville on 22 December. The page names no holder; Cliopatria's Almohad shape covers Seville until 1240. The page also lists Alicante among the 1248 acquisitions (absorbed 1266).

ledger.counterpart: Muslim rulers of Jerez (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1261: Alfonso X captures Jerez. 'In 1261 Alfonso X captured Jerez.' The page also has him invade the Algarve and return it to Portugal 'In 1263' (Treaty of Badajoz 1267); no shape holds the Algarve.
1262: Niebla's client status ends in annexation ('Niebla in 1262' absorbed).
1262: Alfonso X annexes Niebla.
1264: the Mudéjar revolt breaks out. The Murcia page: '1264-1266 Mudéjar revolt', 'conquest by Aragon and ensuing return to Castile'; the Ferdinand III page counts Murcia absorbed 'in 1264'.
1266: the revolt and the Aragonese interlude end; Murcia returns to Castile.
1266: the protectorate of Murcia ends. Infobox 'Annexed by Castile: 1266'.
1266: the Kingdom of Murcia is annexed by Castile ('Annexed by Castile: 1266'); Alicante's absorption is dated 1266 on the Ferdinand III page.
1292: Castile captures Tarifa in October 1292 and keeps it (Emirate page). The page does not name the holder; the Marinids had occupied Tarifa in 1275.
1296: Aragon invades the Kingdom of Murcia. The Torrellas page: Aragon conquered Murcia 'between 1296 and 1301'; James also invaded the Lordship of Villena.

1304: the Treaty of Torrellas (9 August 1304) awards Aragon 'many cities north of the Segura'; Castile is 'restored' the Kingdom of Murcia except the part conquered earlier, and James retained a portion of Villena. The land is my reading: the page names no city; Muntaner's chronicle names Alicante, Orihuela, Elche, Elda, Novelda and Almansa as Aragon's demands.
1305: the border is finalised, 'the following year' (Treaty of Elche).

1309: Castile takes Gibraltar. 'In July 1309 the Castilians laid siege to both Algeciras and Gibraltar'; 'Gibraltar's Nasrid defenders surrendered after a month'. Marinid recapture in 1333 (June 1333 relief force too late).

region.text: Olvera, Pruna, Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime (no gazetteer entries)

ledger.note: 1327: Alfonso XI takes Olvera and its neighbours from Granada. Muhammad IV page: 'the capture of Olvera, in June 1327'; 'Subsequently, Alfonso conquered Pruna, followed by the nearby Ayamonte and Torre Alháquime' (no year of their own, so 1327 for these three is read from the sequence; hence confidence 2). These are the Olvera end of the five cells Cliopatria moves to Castile only in 1333 (replaces the earlier confidence-1 event of 1333, which the Alfonso XI page could not date; re-dated by the eu-12-l repair, 2026-10-25). The cells' coordinates are my reading (no gazetteer entries).

1330: Alfonso XI takes Teba. Muhammad IV page: the siege ran July to August 1330 and 'the fortress surrendered on 30 August'; the Emirate page: 'culminating in the successful siege of Teba in 1330'. Teba is the eastern cell of the five that Cliopatria moves to Castile in 1333 (my reading of the shape). Re-dated from 1333 by the eu-12-l repair.

1333: the Marinids retake Gibraltar. Abu al-Hasan page: 'On 17 June 1333, Vasco Perez surrendered Gibraltar after agreeing terms with Abd al-Malik' and 'In 1333 he captured Gibraltar from the Castilians'. History of Gibraltar: the Castilian relief force arrived in June 1333 and 'the starving inhabitants of Gibraltar had already surrendered to the Moors of Fez'; the Emirate page: 'It besieged Gibraltar and captured it in June.' Mirrors marinid-sultanate /ledger/14. Castile holds Gibraltar again only from August 1462. (Added by the eu-12-l repair, 2026-10-25, after the review found the loss missing.)

region.text: Priego and Alcalá la Real, captured in 1342

ledger.note: 1342: Castile captures Priego and Alcalá la Real (Emirate page, paraphrased).

region.text: 'On 26 March 1344 the city surrendered and was incorporated into the Crown of Castile'

ledger.note: 1344: Algeciras surrenders after the siege begun on 3 August 1342. Granada's envoy brought the king's offer on 2 March; the terms were an annual tribute of twelve thousand doubloons and a ten-year truce. Previous holder: the Marinids. The siege page: 'In 1329 the city was taken over by the King of Morocco, who made it the capital of his European domains' and 'The city was the capital and the main port of the European territory of the Marinid Empire'; the Emirate page has Muhammad IV cede 'Ronda and Algeciras again in 1327 and 1328, respectively'. Cliopatria draws it in Granada. (Counterpart corrected from emirate-of-granada by the eu-12-l review, 2026-10-25.)
1357: Castile penetrates Aragon and conquers Tarazona on 9 March; truce arranged on 8 May. The war runs 1356-1369.
1361: the peace of Terrer (18 May 1361): conquered places and castles were returned to their original lords (paraphrase of the page).

region.text: Tarazona again, Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre, Alicante, Caudete, Elda, Gandia

ledger.note: 1363: Castile again occupies Tarazona and takes Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre, Almenara, Xiva and Bunyol, and in Valencia 'Alicante, Caudete, Elda, Gandia, and other places'. The peace of Morvedre (2 July 1363) did not end the war; the siege of Orihuela failed in 1364.

1369: the war ends with Peter's fall: 'The war lasted from 1356 to 1369, prolonged because Peter of Castile lost his throne to Henry of Trastámara.' The page does not say when Castile left each town; Cliopatria holds them to 1374. The pages disagree on the end: the Peter IV of Aragon page says of the war 'It ended in 1375 with the Treaty of Almazan, without a winner due to the Black Death and several natural disasters', and crown-of-aragon /ledger/43 ends the contest in 1375; this dossier keeps 1369 as the end of the fighting (the War of the Two Peters page, which does not mention Almazan) and its keyframes follow. A reader who prefers 1375 should also restore Cliopatria's 1363 shape to 1374.
1369: Muhammad V of Granada recaptures Algeciras from Castile.

1370: Biscay joins the Crown. The Crown page's table of territorial gains lists '1370: Biscay'. Cliopatria's 1236 shape already reaches the Biscay coast, so the cells are drawn from the start; the date is the lordship's union with the Crown.

1402: Jean de Béthencourt and Gadifer de la Salle land on Lanzarote 'in the summer of 1402'. Béthencourt 'became a vassal of the Castilian King' (the page gives no year); the seigneurial phase runs c.1402-1477.
1405: Fuerteventura ('The conquest of the island was completed in 1405 with the surrender of the native kings') and El Hierro ('took place in 1405') are taken.

1407: Zahara passes to Castile. Zahara de la Sierra page: 'It was ruled by Arabs until 1407.' The page does not name the conqueror (the Infante Ferdinand is not on it) or say that the ruler was Granada; both are my reading, hence confidence 2. Cliopatria's Crown shapes never hold the town, so no shape changes. Closes the earlier gap: the 1481 loss below had no gain before it. Setenil, said by the earlier author to fall in the same campaign, is on no page opened.
1410: Ferdinand, co-regent of Castile, conquers Antequera, whence his surname. The Emirate page dates a war with Castile 'between 1405 and 1410'.

region.text: 'Moorish rule over Gibraltar came to an end in August 1462'

ledger.note: 1462: a small Castilian force led by Alonso de Arcos, governor of Tarifa, takes Gibraltar; the garrison surrenders to Juan Alonso, 'now the first Duke of Medina Sidonia'.

1481: Granada seizes Zahara. 'Granada launched a surprise attack against Zahara on 26 December 1481' and the town fell. Cliopatria's Crown shapes never held it, so no shape changes; the mirror of the Granada dossier's gain. Castilian before this: Zahara de la Sierra page, 'It was ruled by Arabs until 1407' (gain of 1407 above); Castile retook it in 1483.

1482: La Gomera appears in Cliopatria's Castile shape. The Canary page: it 'was not taken in battle but was incorporated' into the Peraza-Herrera fiefdom and was ceded in 1477 to the couple's son; page silent on a date, so 1482 is the shape's. Re-checked (eu-12-l repair): the La Gomera page gives only 'Many natives took refuge in this sacred territory in 1489' and 'it was there that the conquest of La Gomera ended'; no incorporation year, so 1482 stays the shape's.

1482: the Granada War begins with Alhama. 'The seizure of Alhama and its subsequent royal endorsement is usually said to be the formal beginning of the Granada War' (infobox: February 1482 to 2 January 1492).

1482: the tribute that kept Granada a vassal stops with the war. The page: Granadans paid tribute to Castile to avoid attack (paraphrase of the page); Granada attacked Zahara on 26 December 1481. Month and form of the break are my reading.
1482: Castile takes Alhama de Granada; reinforcements on 28 April averted its retaking and Ferdinand took command there on 14 May 1482.

1483: Castile retakes Zahara. Zahara de la Sierra page: 'It was finally captured by Castilian troops under command of Rodrigo Ponce de León, Duke of Cádiz in 1483.' (The page also has 'It was recaptured by the Emirate of Granada in 1481'.) Cliopatria's Crown shapes never hold the town, so no shape changes.
1483: Gran Canaria is won. The first landing was on 24 June 1478; 'On 29 April 1483 Guayarmina Semidán surrendered at Ansite Fortress'.

region.text: Ronda, then Marbella 'a base of the Granadan fleet'

ledger.note: 1485: Ronda 'fell to him after fifteen days' and 'Ronda's fall allowed Marbella ... to come into Christian hands next' (1485). The Ronda year is my reading from the sequence; the page gives no month.
1486: Loja falls after a 'second Loja siege'; the page names the siege year, not the surrender.
1487: Vélez-Málaga capitulates on 27 April.

region.text: 'a siege that lasted from 7 May 1487 until 18 August 1487'

ledger.note: 1487: Málaga falls on 18 August after a siege that began on 7 May.
1487: the western campaign ends with Málaga on 18 August 1487.
1489: Castile besieges Baza; the siege began in 1489 and, 'after six months, al-Zagal surrendered'.
1489: Baza surrenders to Castile after six months.

region.text: 'negotiated the surrender of Almería and Guadix'

ledger.note: 1489: Almería and Guadix surrender through al-Zagal. The Emirate page gives no year; 1489 is a bridging judgment after Baza.
1489: the eastern campaign is treated as ended with the surrenders; bridging judgment, the page gives no end date for it.
1491: the siege of Granada begins. 'An eight-month siege of Granada began in April 1491'.
1492: Granada surrenders. The Treaty of Granada 'was signed on November 25, 1491'; 'the city capitulated on January 2, 1492'. Cliopatria's Crown shape gains 53 cells in 1492.
1492: the Granada War ends on 2 January.
1493: La Palma is won. 'The official date for the end of the conquest is given as 3 May 1493.'

1496: Santo Domingo is founded. 'On Hispaniola, the city of Santo Domingo was founded in 1496 by Christopher Columbus's brother Bartholomew Columbus'. The Columbus landing was on 12 October 1492 and the bull Inter caetera is dated 4 May 1493; the extent of the claim on land is my reading.
1496: Tenerife is won. 'the conquest of Tenerife ended on July 25, 1496', with the Treaty of Los Realejos.

1497: Melilla is conquered. 'It had conquered Melilla in 1497' (Spanish Empire page); the Crown page's text gives 1497. The holder is not named on either page; the Wattasids are the neighbour Cliopatria lists.

1502: Cliopatria adds 22 cells of western Hispaniola. Page silent: no page opened dates the western settlement. Re-checked (eu-12-l repair): the Captaincy General of Santo Domingo page has only 'In 1502, Nicolás de Ovando replaced de Bobadilla as governor' and the 1493 and 1496 foundings; nothing on the west.

region.text: Mers El Kébir (Mazalquivir), 'captured it in 1505 under Cardinal Cisneros'

ledger.note: 1505: the Spanish take Mers el-Kebir. Mers El Kébir page: 'The Spanish, who named it Mazalquivir, captured it in 1505 under Cardinal Cisneros.' The page names neither the crown nor the previous holder; Castile (the crown Cisneros served) and the Zayyanids of Tlemcen (the holder of Oran in 1509, Spanish Oran page) are my reading, hence confidence 2. zayyanid-dynasty /ledger/11 dates the capture 1505 too. Replaces the earlier confidence-1 event of 1507 (Cliopatria's year for the Oran cells), by the eu-12-l repair.

region.text: 'Juan Ponce de León conquered Puerto Rico (1508)'

ledger.note: 1508: Juan Ponce de León conquers Puerto Rico.

1509: the Spanish take Oran. Spanish Oran page: 'Spanish conquest: 1509' (infobox) and 'The conquest was carried out by the Spanish Empire on the Kingdom of Tlemcen.' The page says the Spanish Empire, not the Crown of Castile; Cliopatria draws Oran in Castile's shape from 1507, and attributing it to Castile is my reading (confidence 2). Mirrors zayyanid-dynasty /ledger/12. Replaces the earlier confidence-1 event of 1507, by the eu-12-l repair.

1509: the first Spanish settlement on Jamaica. Colony of Santiago page: 'In 1509 the first Spanish settlement on the island was founded near St Ann's Bay' and Diego Columbus 'instructed conquistador Juan de Esquivel to formally occupy Jamaica in his name'; Esquivel is governor from 1510 (infobox 1510-1514). The page does not name the Crown of Castile; that is my reading, hence confidence 2. Cliopatria's 1512 shape includes all of Jamaica, three years after this date. (Re-dated from 1512, confidence 1, by the eu-12-l repair; the Spanish Empire page, which was silent, is no longer the source.)

region.text: 'Santa María la Antigua del Darién ... settled by Vasco Núñez de Balboa in 1510'

ledger.note: 1510: Santa María la Antigua del Darién is settled, the first mainland settlement (Castilla de Oro); 'In 1513, Balboa crossed the Isthmus of Panama'.

1510: Cliopatria's 1512 shape holds the Béjaïa coast and Tripoli. The page dates the North African conquests only as 'between 1505 and 1510' (page silent on town and year); the Hafsids are the neighbour Cliopatria lists from 1512. Re-checked (eu-12-l repair): the Spanish Tripoli page has 'Tripoli was captured by a Spanish force led by Count Pedro Navarro in 1510' and the status 'Territory of the Spanish Empire under the jurisdiction of Sicily', that is the Aragonese side, so Tripoli is dated but not Castilian; Béjaïa is on no page opened. Confidence stays 1 for the Castilian attribution.

region.text: the eastern end of Cuba that Cliopatria's 1512 shape holds

ledger.note: 1511: Spanish settlement of eastern Cuba begins. Diego Velázquez de Cuéllar page: 'Velázquez sailed for Cuba in January 1511 and landed at a small harbor in the native province of Mayci' and 'The first Spanish settlement, Baracoa, was established on the northeast corner of the island by August 1511'; Bayamo 1513, Trinidad, Sancti Spiritus and Havana 1514, Santiago de Cuba July 1515. Which of those the 41 cells of Cliopatria's 1512 shape cover is my reading, hence confidence 2. (Re-dated from 1512, confidence 1, by the eu-12-l repair.)
1512: Castile conquers Navarre. The Crown page's table lists '1512: Navarre' and its infobox the annexation in 1515; the Spanish Empire page: 'Conquest of Navarre: 1512–29'.

1515: the Crown of Castile passes into the Spanish monarchy. Charles I becomes co-monarch with Joanna I on 13 March 1516 (list of monarchs; the Crown page: 23 January 1516); the Crown of Castile itself lasts to 1716 on the Crown page, but the map follows Cliopatria's Spain row from 1516.

wars.name: Reconquest campaigns of Ferdinand III
wars.outcome: Córdoba (1236), Murcia by the pact of Alcaraz (1243), Arjona (1244), Jaén (March 1246) and Seville (22 December 1248) pass to Castile; Granada becomes a vassal.
wars.note: The Ferdinand III page also gives the Treaty of Almizra (26 March 1244) with Aragon.

wars.name: Mudéjar revolt of 1264-1266
wars.outcome: The revolt was put down; Aragon conquered Murcia and returned it to Castile; annexed 1266.

wars.name: Aragonese invasion of Murcia and the Treaty of Torrellas
wars.outcome: Aragon conquered Murcia between 1296 and 1301; the Treaty of Torrellas of 9 August 1304 awarded Aragon many cities north of the Segura and restored the rest of the Kingdom of Murcia to Castile; border finalised in 1305.

wars.name: Siege of Algeciras (1342-1344)
wars.outcome: Algeciras surrendered on 26 March 1344; Priego and Alcalá la Real fell in 1342 (Emirate page); ten-year truce and a tribute of twelve thousand doubloons from Granada.

wars.name: War of the Two Peters

zones.text: the Aragonese and Valencian lands Cliopatria gives Castile in 1363 (58 cells around Valencia, Zaragoza and Teruel)

wars.outcome: Castile occupied Tarazona (1357, 1363) and, in 1363, Cariñena, Teruel, Segorbe, Morvedre and Alicante; the peaces of Terrer (18 May 1361) and Morvedre (2 July 1363) did not end it; it ended with Peter's death at Montiel in 1369.
wars.note: The Castilian Civil War began in 1366 and Henry of Trastámara killed Peter; Granada supported Peter.

wars.name: Castilian-Granadan war of 1405-1410
wars.outcome: Ferdinand of Antequera conquered Antequera in 1410.
wars.note: The 1405-1410 span is the Emirate page's.

wars.name: Conquest of the Canary Islands
belligerents: the Guanche kings of the Canary Islands
wars.outcome: Béthencourt took Lanzarote (1402), Fuerteventura and El Hierro (1405); the Crown conquered Gran Canaria (surrender 29 April 1483), La Palma (3 May 1493) and Tenerife (25 July 1496).
wars.note: Portugal's claims (a 1341 expedition, grants of 1370) are on the page; no Castilian-Portuguese war is dated there.

wars.name: Granada War

zones.text: the western half of the emirate that Cliopatria moves from Granada to Castile between its 1463 and 1487 shapes
the eastern emirate around Baza, Guadix and Almería
the city of Granada and its Vega

wars.outcome: Castilian-Aragonese victory: Alhama (1482), Ronda and Marbella (1485), Loja (1486), Vélez-Málaga and Málaga (1487), Baza and the east (1489), the Treaty of Granada (25 November 1491) and the surrender on 2 January 1492.

wars.name: War of the Castilian Succession
wars.outcome: Isabella and Ferdinand prevailed; the Crown page dates the war's end to 1479, the year of the personal union of the crowns.
wars.note: No territorial change on the page; the Treaty of Alcáçovas (1479) is not on any page opened. Cliopatria's personal union row for Aragon and Castile (1475-1515) is an umbrella, not territory.

wars.name: Spanish conquest of North African posts
wars.outcome: Several towns and outposts on the North African coast were conquered and occupied by Castile between 1505 and 1510; Melilla in 1497.
wars.note: The page dates none of the towns individually.

wars.name: Conquest of Navarre
wars.outcome: Castile conquered Navarre in 1512 and annexed it in 1515 (Crown page); the Spanish Empire page dates the conquest 1512-1529.

certainty.note: The Muslim and Portuguese frontiers are approximate and moved by sieges. Exceptions that are sharp: the Murcia-Aragon line delineated by the Treaty of Almizra (26 March 1244) and the Aragonese frontier finalised at Torrellas and Elche (1304-1305). The Canary and American cells are coasts and islands, sharp by nature but placed by Cliopatria, not by a survey.

notes:
Sixteen pages were opened for this dossier (budget up to 9): seven beyond the budget are shared with the Granada dossier (Emirate of Granada, Granada War, Siege of Algeciras, History of Gibraltar, Ferdinand I of Aragon) or give capital and rulers (Kingdom of Castile, List of Castilian monarchs); the Alfonso XI page was opened for the 1333 strip and was silent. Cliopatria's 25 shapes (311 k to 536 k km2) mix three things: the Iberian crown (1236-1492), the Canaries (from 1402) and the Americas and North African posts (from 1497).

Cliopatria rows to correct or split: (1) 1241 puts Seville and the Jaén district in Castile seven and five years before the pages (Arjona 1244, Jaén March 1246, Seville 22 December 1248); corrected by four new keyframes. (2) 1250 draws the Murcian protectorate (1243-1266) as Castile's own land; the vassal events carry the difference. (3) 1363-1374: the Aragonese occupation runs five years past the page's end of the war (1369) and eight Granada-edge cells are given back with no page; corrected by an adjust and a 1370 keyframe. (4) The Gibraltar and Algeciras cells sit in Granada's shape throughout; the ledger has Gibraltar Castilian 1309-1333 and 1462, Algeciras 1344-1369. (5) 1333 and 1285 frontier cells have no page. (6) The 1497-1512 shapes bundle Castilian and Aragonese conquests (Tripoli, Béjaïa) and overseas cells: Cliopatria lacks a Crown of Aragon Mediterranean overlay for these; the Navarre and Caribbean cells are right in kind.

States needing a dossier or a decision from another group: lordship-of-biscay (Biscay joins 1370), 'Muslim rulers of Jerez' (no state), the Kingdom of Navarre after 1428 (Cliopatria's row ends 1428; the Navarre dossier belongs to eu-12), the Crown of Aragon dossier should carry the mirror of the 1296-1305 and 1357-1369 events and the personal union of 1479; Marinid sultanate (af-02) for the 1275-1292 Strait events. The Kingdom of Spain dossier starts in March 1516.

Unsettled: the vassalage of Granada has three start dates on the pages (1238 Ferdinand III page, 1243 Nasrid page, March 1246 Treaty of Jaén); the Algarve captured by Alfonso X and returned 'In 1263' (Alfonso X page, ambiguous year of capture) is not in the ledger; the Treaty of Alcáçovas (1479) and the Treaty of Tordesillas (7 June 1494) are not on a page opened as territorial events; Cuba (Velázquez, undated on the Spanish Empire page) is not in Cliopatria's shape.

Gazetteer names needed (coordinates used instead): places Jerez de la Frontera, Alcalá la Real, Priego de Córdoba, Antequera, Ronda, Guadix, Baza, Tarifa, Vélez-Málaga, Alhama de Granada, Tarazona, Orihuela, Niebla, Zahara; 'Vizcaya' (admin1 Biscay) is checked in the resolve run.

Repair pass, 2026-10-25 (eu-12-l, after the adversarial review). (1) Blocking finding fixed: the loss of Gibraltar to the Marinids on 17 June 1333 (Abu al-Hasan page; History of Gibraltar: 'had already surrendered to the Moors of Fez'), so Castile holds Gibraltar 1309 to June 1333 and again from August 1462. (2) The confidence-1 Olvera-Teba event of 1333 is replaced by Olvera and its neighbours (June 1327) and Teba (30 August 1330) from the Muhammad IV of Granada page; keyframe 1333 is now adjust. (3) Oran 1507 is replaced by Mers el-Kebir 1505 (Mers El Kébir page) and Oran 1509 (Spanish Oran page); keyframe 1507 is adjust. (4) Zahara gains 1407 (page: 'ruled by Arabs until 1407') and 1483. (5) Jamaica 1509 and eastern Cuba 1511 replace the confidence-1 events of 1512. (6) kingdom-of-leon is dropped from the predecessors; its land arrives through kingdom-of-castile. (7) Disagreement kept: the War of the Two Peters page ends the war in 1369 and Peter IV of Aragon page in 1375 (Treaty of Almazan); this dossier keeps 1369 and says so on the event. (8) Still undated after the extra pages: La Gomera (page gives 1489 as the end of the conquest), western Hispaniola (Ovando 1502 only), Béjaïa, Almería and Guadix (Muhammad XIII page silent), and the Algarve (Treaty of Badajoz page: 20 September 1264 renunciation, signed 16 February 1267; it describes no Castilian conquest, so no event was written).
